clue.text: Kind of 16 in colour

indicators.note: the word for a fellow sits inside the word for colour, so in signals a container

parts.note: a hue is a colour or shade
the answer to 16 across is a word for a fellow, so this cross-reference stands for man

explanation.surface: Asks what sort of chap appears in a particular colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 points to the answer at 16 across, a slang word for a fellow, which here means MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A humane person is compassionate, which is what being kind means.

clue.text: Plant producing medicine woman takes in twice the average

parts.note: her stands for a woman

indicators.note: the word for twice takes in the average, enclosing it

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat
par is the average or normal standard

explanation.surface: A healer's female practitioner absorbs double the normal amount.
explanation.walkthrough: Bis is Latin for twice, seen on music scores calling for a repeat; par is the normal level, as in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb Paris is a woodland plant once used in herbal remedies, though poisonous.

clue.text: Meek lieges alternately entered the fray

indicators.note: alternately means taking every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Gentle vassals took turns joining the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused fight, a free-for-all, which is a fray.

clue.text: This could settle me in post

definitions.text: This could settle me in post

indicators.note: settle suggests letters being arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A way to get myself a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could settle' rearranges ME IN POST; the whole clue doubles as a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring relatives for jobs is how someone might be installed in a post.

clue.text: Chinamen, for instance, are nuts

definitions.meaning: in cricket a chinaman is an unusual delivery from a left-arm wrist spinner
nuts as a plural noun means eccentric or crazy people

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a chinaman is a left-arm wrist-spinner's unorthodox delivery, hence an odd ball; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric, crazy people can be called nuts or oddballs, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Drag baskets of crackers into the mess

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Pulling baskets of biscuits into the army dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' rearranges DRAG BASKETS OF; 'into the' is a link. Crackers and mess look like food and a canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's breakfast is a British idiom for a muddle or botched job.

clue.text: Unexpectedly visited dismal pub — I say!

indicators.note: I say tells us the words are spoken out, giving their sound

parts.note: blue means dismal and an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a gloomy drinking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow in is informal for to arrive casually or without warning.

clue.text: Enjoy a nip? Willingly!

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
a nip is a small drink, a shot

explanation.surface: Asking someone whether they fancy a drink, and getting an eager yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like a shot means at once and eagerly, willingly.

clue.text: Seeing start of service in church

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of service

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Watching the opening of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing that and since both mean because or given that, as conjunctions.

clue.text: Trained tree to face west without a single setback

indicators.note: without tells us a letter is dropped from the reversed tree
in an across clue facing west means reading right to left, a backwards reading

parts.note: an espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: Gardening instructions for turning a trained tree round.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPALIER turned westward gives REILAPSE; 'without a single' then removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a return to illness after improvement, a kind of setback.

clue.text: "Blooming" —— a euphemism to express anger over learning not one ology

parts.note: eff stands in for a swear word, as in effing
lore is traditional learning

indicators.note: not means the letter for one is left out of the science

parts.note: an ology is jocular for any science
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A coy word for swearing about a scientific subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link: in a down clue the pieces are stacked. 'not one' removes I from SCIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Efflorescence is the process of flowering, so it means blooming.

clue.text: Lady's family going after grand fruit

indicators.note: the lady's family is placed after the letter for grand, so going after orders the pieces

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for grand, a thousand
her is the possessive for a lady
kin means family or relations

explanation.surface: A noblewoman's relatives come after the grandee in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A gherkin is a small cucumber, botanically a fruit, usually pickled.

clue.text: Place to consume tuck

parts.note: PL is the standard abbreviation for Place in street addresses
to eat is to consume food

explanation.surface: A spot where one goes to eat tuck, the British schoolchild's word for snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck' looks like food (British school slang for sweets and snacks), but it is the dressmaker's fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck and a pleat are both folds stitched into fabric, near-synonyms in dressmaking.

clue.text: If cabaret is out of shape-— and fashion --…

indicators.note: letters that are out of shape have lost their order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cabaret has lost its form and its style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out of shape' rearranges the letters of IF CABARET; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to make or construct something, which is what fashion means as a verb.

clue.text: … again, find right sort of entertainment, that's always around

indicators.note: the word for always goes around the entertainment, so around signals a container

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
a disco is a dance party, a kind of entertainment

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: finding again a form of entertainment that never goes away.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the previous clue, so 'again, find' is the definition; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To find again is the literal meaning of the verb built from the prefix re- and discover.

clue.text: Motherland's punishment

parts.note: split into mother as an animal's dam and land as a nation, the two parts run together

explanation.surface: A country's penalty for wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the first word: a dam is an animal's mother, and a land is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is eternal punishment in hell.

clue.text: Crack revealed in short section of book

indicators.note: short means the word for a book section is cut down, its end trimmed off

parts.note: a chapter is a section of a book

explanation.surface: A fault in a book discovered in a brief part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed in' is a link; 'short' trims TER from CHAPTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapped skin is cracked, and a chap is a crack in skin caused by cold.

clue.text: Teacher of gym eager to be taken in directly

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym

indicators.note: the eager word is to be taken in by the word for directly

parts.note: due means directly, as in due north
agog means eager and excited

explanation.surface: A gym instructor eager to be admitted straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: Due means directly in phrases like due north; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a teacher, often a strict or pedantic one.

clue.text: To show respect, first I must abandon attitude, and spar

indicators.note: first places the respectful gesture at the top of this down answer, ahead of the rest

parts.note: to bow is to show respect

indicators.note: abandon means the letter is dropped from the word for attitude

parts.note: spirit means attitude or mood
the letter I as printed in the clue

explanation.surface: Advice to be respectful, drop one's attitude, and box.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIRIT losing an I gives SPRIT; 'and' is a link. 'spar' looks like boxing but is a ship's pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsprit is a spar projecting forward from a ship's bow.

clue.text: A little problem, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells us the word is chosen for how it is spoken

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Something is a minor difficulty, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Some means a certain amount, as in have some cake, a little of it.

clue.text: Jump the broomstick —-hop it

definitions.meaning: jumping the broomstick is an old phrase meaning to marry, to tie the knot
hop it is British slang for go away, used rudely

explanation.walkthrough: Getting knotted can mean getting married, and get knotted is a rude British dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works literally as marrying and idiomatically as a brusque telling someone to clear off.

clue.text: Ship stores fish in jars

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so the fish goes within the ship

parts.note: SS is steamship
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A ship's supplies include fish preserved in jars.
explanation.definitionFit: Jars as a verb means jolts or rattles, as shakes does.

clue.text: Dance put together by three 16's not quietly

indicators.note: quietly is P, piano in music, and not removes it each time

parts.note: the answer to 16 across, a word for crack or fellow, taken three times over

explanation.surface: A dance assembled by three fellows making noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is the word for a fellow; three of them each lose P (piano, quiet in music).
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Leader of crew talking —"What crew?"

indicators.note: talking tells us the word is said aloud

parts.note: a cox steers and leads a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A boat's coxswain asks which rowers are meant.
explanation.walkthrough: In the definition, crew is the past tense of crow, so it asks which birds crowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosters crow, so the birds that crew in the morning are male fowl.

clue.text: Youth needing special outfit

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing, as in rig-out

explanation.surface: A young person who needs special clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprig is an old, somewhat dismissive word for a young man, a stripling.

clue.text: One horn strange feature of this

definitions.text: One horn strange feature of this

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single horn is an odd feature of a certain animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges I and HORN; the whole clue also defines the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian rhinoceros has a single horn, its striking feature.

clue.text: Smart bloke, easily scared

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish
Ken is a man's name, standing for any bloke

explanation.surface: A stylish man who frightens easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken as an adjective means cowardly, readily frightened.

clue.text: Retire, and start to go a different road

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed, retire for the night

indicators.note: start to signals the opening letter of the word go

explanation.surface: Going to bed, and setting off on another route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'a' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning is a side road branching off, another road to take.

clue.text: Threatening one used to nursing home in hiding

indicators.note: the word for home is concealed within the nurse, so in hiding is a container

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone experienced in care work menacingly concealing themselves in a home.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse, and 'home' gives IN as in staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something menacing or suggesting harm.

clue.text: Fondle breast, for one

definitions.meaning: to fondle is to caress gently
breaststroke is a swimming style, an example of this word

explanation.walkthrough: Breast is short for breaststroke, a swimming style.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle caress and a swimming style are both covered by the same word.
